title: tier record
description: What one inference tier was measured to do. Contains no model name in any field the router reads: `serves` is provenance for a human, and every routing decision is taken from the measured fields. A field whose value was not measured is null, never zero and never a published figure -- this deployment has seen an engine advertise 7-14x more reusable cache than it had and a rate card price a model 17x wrong.

id.description: Stable key the router uses. Opaque; not parsed.

serves.description: Human-readable provenance only. The router must not branch on anything in here.

provenance.description: Where the numbers came from, so a decision is reproducible from versioned inputs.

adapter.description: Protocol facts, measured separately from task ability. Conflating the two cost one tier 42% of its actions once.

compliance.description: Fractions of parsed steps, from a measured run.

restrictions.description: Combinations the endpoint refuses, as capability facts rather than as 400s discovered at runtime.

price_card.description: Per request shape, because the cache discount attaches to the shape and not to the text: identical content sent as one long message hit 0% where a growing conversation hit 99.9%.

source.description: Catalog and retrieval, or the measurement that produced it. Published figures are inadmissible where a measured one exists.

cached_in.description: null when the tier does not report cached tokens. Never coerced to zero: unmeasured is not free.

hourly_fixed_usd.description: Non-null makes this tier's effective rate max(token rates, hourly / realised tasks per hour), recomputed hourly.

reusable_cache_tokens.description: Measured by interposing traffic between populate and reuse, not read from the engine's advertised capacity.

latency.description: A distribution, because chains stack tails and a mean hides the arrangement that misses its SLO.

concurrency_when_measured.description: A latency figure taken at low concurrency is optimistic in exactly the regime where the cost figure is realistic.

reliability.description: The term that reordered the arrangements. Cost of a call is bill + p/(1-p) * mean spend sunk before death, so an unreliable tier that dies late is dearer than its bill.

families.description: Per traffic family, the measured outcome and whether this tier is nested under the family's reference tier. Nesting is a per-family, per-pair property re-certified at admission, never a global assumption.

suite.description: The frozen benchmark set and its selection rule.

runs_per_item.description: One run measures an episode, not a capability.

counterexamples.description: Items this tier solved and the reference did not. Non-zero withdraws the chain assumption for this family.

eligibility.description: Hard constraints, checked before any cost arithmetic.
